function: Diffusion model completes the full BS-RIS-user cascaded channel from a partial estimate, and a decision Transformer outputs RIS phase shifts that maximize the data rate (p. 5-8).
system: Downlink: BS with 4-antenna ULA, passive reflecting RIS with 64, 256 or 512 elements, single-antenna user, blocked direct link, quasi-static flat fading; band not stated (p. 4, 10).
method: Conditional denoising diffusion model with spatial-feature Transformer (supervised noise prediction); decision Transformer trained offline on near-optimal RL trajectories, then few-shot fine-tuned (last layer) in new environments (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: spatially correlated complex Gaussian channels from an isotropic-scattering model, default settings of the authors' earlier paper [21]; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements (p. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Pretraining on the default environment of [21]; new environments simulated by changing channel parameters and BS-RIS distances, with few-shot fine-tuning of the DT; N=64/256/512 at 5/15/30 dB (p. 9-11).
baselines: Channel: random-channel completion (RC, non-learned). Beamforming: DT with random channel (RCDT), DT with perfect channel (PCDT, upper bound), DM-PPO, DM-DDPG, RC-PPO; no SDR or alternating optimization (p. 10-11).
metrics: NMSE of the generated channel versus SNR and mask ratio; effective data rate (rate minus estimation overhead) versus SNR, mask ratio and epochs (p. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 10: "We utilize the default parameter settings in [21] as the simulation environment for offline pretraining" - the channel is the paper's own spatially correlated Gaussian model (p. 5); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "we change the channel parameters and BS-RIS distances to simulate different wireless environments"; p. 9: "This requires additional fine-tuning of the pretrained model" with few-shot samples from the new environment.
q3_support: p. 10: "we use the random channel (RC) approach, where the remaining channels are randomly generated based on the unmasked RIS elements" (non-learned, NMSE); p. 11: "the performance of DEDT surpasses RL methods by approximately 7.5%" over DM-PPO, DM-DDPG, RC-PPO.
q4_support: p. 11: "reaching convergence in approximately 300 epochs" is a training-convergence count; no FLOPs, parameter count, runtime or complexity order is reported, and the savings are qualitative (p. 2: "reduces the computational overhead for CSI acquisition").
q5_support: p. 10: "We utilize the default parameter settings in [21] as the simulation environment for offline pretraining" - the data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Area 3 rather than 2: the main metric is the effective data rate of the RIS phase-shift policy (problem P, p. 4; Figs. 6-10), while the diffusion channel acquisition (NMSE, Fig. 5) supports it. q2 rests on the few-shot fine-tuning of the DT in new environments (p. 9) and the claim of results in new environments (p. 11); the paper does not tabulate the pretraining and test environment parameters. q3 is weak: the only non-learned baseline is random channel completion (RC, Fig. 5), with no SDR, alternating optimization, LS or MMSE comparison, and the learned baselines are standard PPO and DDPG applied to the same problem (p. 11); reviewer to confirm. PCDT and RCDT are variants of the proposed method and are not counted.
